body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students retell a short story in order, using first, next and last (RL.1.2).
- Students name the characters, the setting and the main events of a story (RL.1.3).
- Students ask and answer questions about key details in a story read aloud (RL.1.1).

MATERIALS
- The Little Seed (student overview) printed large or projected
- Three sequence cards labeled First, Next, Last
- Crayons and drawing paper, or tablets for drawing
- A story map: Who? Where? What happened?

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read The Little Seed aloud twice. Point to the sequence cards as you read first, next and last. Ask: who helped the seed?
Day 2: Lesson activity: Who, Where, What Happened. Read the story about Pip the puppy aloud; students answer by speaking.
Day 3: Model a retell of a familiar story using the sequence cards. Students begin Retell The Little Seed.
Day 4: Finish Retell The Little Seed. Share drawings of what happened last and compare them with a partner.
Day 5: Assessment: Retell a Story. Read The Lost Mitten aloud twice, then students record and draw their retell.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: give students the three sequence cards to hold while they retell, and let them point to pictures.
- Support: accept a retell in the student's home language for the speaking questions, then add the English sentence frame together.
- Stretch: ask students to tell the lesson of the story (what the character learned) and to add a new ending.
- Students who are still learning to draw details can label their picture with one word instead.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week we are listening to stories and telling them back in order. After you read a bedtime story together, ask your child: what happened first, next and last? Who was in the story, and where did it happen? Telling a story back is one of the best ways to build reading comprehension.
